title: The Laws of Manu
author: manu
attributionNote: The text presents itself as the teaching of Manu, the primordial lawgiver, to the sages. Its actual composition is anonymous and cumulative, the work of Brahmanical circles over several centuries.
description: The Laws of Manu is the most influential Sanskrit treatise on dharma: the social order of the four classes and their stages of life, marriage and inheritance, the duties of the king and the conduct of law, purity and food, penance and expiation, and the teaching of transmigration and final release. It shaped Hindu, Buddhist and Southeast Asian legal practice for more than a millennium.
historicalContext: The Manusmriti was compiled in its surviving form around the turn of the era and commented on by Medhatithi, Govindaraja and Kulluka. Georg Bühler's translation, published in the Sacred Books of the East, volume 25 (1886), was the first complete English rendering and remains the standard public-domain edition.
availabilityNote: Complete. All twelve chapters of Bühler's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The translator's notes and the volume's preface and index are not part of the work.
